register.name: Extended Fund Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 26 February 2025 · 40 months · SDR 1,033.92M · second and third reviews completed, 1 October 2026
register.note: SDR 101.96 million (about US$138 million) released on the second and third reviews
register.text: A 40-month IMF Extended Fund Facility of SDR 1,033.92 million (about US$1.4 billion, 360 percent of quota), approved on 26 February 2025. The first review, in June 2025, released SDR 86.16 million (about US$118 million); the second and third reviews, completed together in October 2026, released SDR 101.96 million (about US$138 million).

register.name: Programme to Accelerate Learning through Digital Innovation (AprendES)
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Approved 31 March 2026 · Program-for-Results · P511960 · Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
register.note: The first results-based loan introduced in El Salvador
register.text: A World Bank loan of US$501 million to improve learning in basic education, with a focus on reading and mathematics, teaching with digital resources, assessments and connectivity, in public schools from grades 2 to 11. Its disbursements are tied to results. It serves the education standard, the one furthest from reach.

register.name: Strengthened Financial Intermediation for Employment
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Approved 31 March 2026 · P513645 · to BANDESAL, with a sovereign guarantee · five years
register.note: About 5,000 MSMEs to receive longer-term loans; about 8,300 jobs created or improved, close to 30% for women
register.text: A World Bank loan of US$100 million to the Banco de Desarrollo de la República de El Salvador (BANDESAL), with a sovereign guarantee, for a credit line that lets more micro, small and medium enterprises borrow for longer terms, with a scheme of partial credit guarantees. IFC is to facilitate complementary private investment. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Promoting Job Opportunities and Skills Development
register.text: Skills and jobs for young people.

register.name: Transport and Resilient Infrastructure
register.text: Roads and bridges built to withstand storms.

register.name: RECLIMA: climate resilience in the dry corridor agroecosystems
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · FAO · FP089 · Approved 20 October 2018 · completion date 17 July 2026
register.note: Fully disbursed; a project of US$128 million in all, for 1.3 million people with increased resilience
register.text: Green Climate Fund financing of US$35,849,612, fully disbursed, for a US$128 million project led by FAO that restores and reforests degraded land in El Salvador’s Dry Corridor to protect water sources and recharge aquifers, and helps small-scale farmers withstand climate change. It serves the food and water standards.

register.name: Scholarships for higher and technical studies
register.detail: CABEI · 9 November 2026 · partial scholarships for the first cycle of 2027 · 14 institutions
register.note: For 5,194 young Salvadorans, with psychosocial, academic and vocational support
register.text: CABEI is to allocate up to US$1.725 million to partial scholarships for 5,194 young Salvadorans in higher and technical education enrolled in the first cycle of 2027, with psychosocial, academic and vocational support. The Dirección de Integración de El Salvador has signed agreements with 14 higher-education and technical-training institutions to carry it out; it serves the education standard.

register.name: Global credit line to the Fondo Social para la Vivienda, increase
register.detail: CABEI · 28 July 2026 · increase of US$50M · line of US$103.7M in all · social-interest housing
register.note: About 1,250 home loans expected, half for women, benefiting some 3,875 people
register.text: CABEI increased by US$50 million its global credit line to El Salvador’s Fondo Social para la Vivienda, bringing the line to US$103.7 million, for subloans to buy new or used social-interest homes and reduce the housing shortfall. About 1,250 loans are expected, half of them for women; so far the line has lent to 2,403 women and 3,591 men. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Academic and community integration programme for young people
register.detail: IDB · Approved 24 June 2026 · ES-L1175 · sovereign-guaranteed investment loan
register.note: To improve the continuity of young Salvadorans into upper-secondary and post-secondary education
register.text: An IDB investment loan of US$100 million to improve the continuity of young Salvadoran students in upper-secondary and post-secondary education: support services in upper-secondary schools, wider access to post-secondary education and stronger capacity to follow the paths of students after school. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Road Infrastructure and Urban Mobility Programme, Phase II
register.detail: CABEI · Approved 28 April 2026 · RN13W, Atiquizaya to Ahuachapán · northern corridor of the San Salvador ring road
register.note: More than 1.17 million people to benefit; travel times cut by an estimated 45.6% on the sections
register.text: CABEI financing of US$155 million for the second phase of El Salvador’s road infrastructure and urban mobility programme: 7.05 km of the RN13W highway widened to four lanes, 8.17 km of new roads and 30.4 km of cycle lanes, with designs for the northern and eastern corridors of the San Salvador metropolitan ring road. Roads that bring homes closer to work and markets serve the livelihood standard.

register.name: Guluchapa drinking water system, San Salvador metropolitan area
register.detail: CABEI · Approved 25 February 2026 · ANDA · treatment plant of 650 litres per second · 25,000 household connections
register.note: More than 156,000 people to benefit; coverage in the area to rise from 61.5% to 100%
register.text: CABEI financing of US$185 million for the Republic of El Salvador, carried out by ANDA, for new water intake works, a treatment plant at Joya Grande of 650 litres per second, 37.14 km of distribution pipes, 25,000 household connections and a water quality laboratory. It is to benefit more than 156,000 people in seven districts of San Salvador and La Paz, and it serves the water standard.

register.name: Programme to Support Macroeconomic and Fiscal Sustainability
register.detail: IDB · Approved 19 March 2025 · ES-L1153 · special development lending · closed
register.note: To ensure fiscal sustainability and improve financial integrity and stability
register.text: An IDB special development loan of US$500 million, with a sovereign guarantee, to strengthen El Salvador’s macroeconomic stability: to ensure fiscal sustainability and to improve the integrity and stability of the financial system. The operation is now closed.

register.name: Credit facility for SMEs, women-led SMEs and green financing, Banco Davivienda Salvadoreño
register.detail: IDB Invest · Approved 25 November 2025 · signed 12 December 2025 · loan of up to eight years · project 15665-01
register.note: A loan of up to US$70 million, which participants may supplement with about US$50 million
register.text: An IDB Invest loan of up to US$70 million, for up to eight years, to Banco Davivienda Salvadoreño to finance small and medium enterprises, SMEs led by women and green financing in El Salvador, with possible technical assistance in digitalisation and innovation. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Financing for MSMEs, Bancoagrícola
register.detail: IFC · 6 November 2025 · US$115M from IFC · US$35M mobilised
register.note: Priority for small businesses led by women and by people over 50
register.text: A US$150 million financing for Bancoagrícola, of which US$115 million from IFC and US$35 million mobilised from others, to expand its lending to formal and informal micro, small and medium enterprises, with priority for small businesses led by women and by people over 50. IFC is also to advise the bank on its MSME credit processes; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Sustainable SME financing, Banco Agrícola
register.detail: IDB Invest · 29 July 2025 · up to US$40M from IDB Invest · up to US$10M from the Canadian Accelerator Fund · US$100M from private investors
register.note: The whole operation; IDB Invest’s own loan is up to US$40 million
register.text: A financing operation of up to US$150 million for Banco Agrícola to expand its lending to small and medium enterprises, particularly for sustainable projects: up to US$40 million from IDB Invest, up to US$10 million from the Canadian Accelerator Fund for Net Zero Emissions and Climate Resilience, and the rest from private investors. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Debt conversion for the conservation of the Lempa river
register.detail: DFC · CAF · JPMorgan · completed 16 October 2024 · US$1bn political risk insurance · US$200M standby letter of credit · 20 years
register.note: Bonds repurchased; US$350 million of the savings go to the Rio Lempa Conservation and Restoration Program over 20 years
register.text: El Salvador repurchased US$1.031 billion of its outstanding bonds at discounts to par, financed by a loan arranged and made by JPMorgan Chase Bank, with US$1 billion of DFC political risk insurance and a US$200 million CAF standby letter of credit. US$350 million of the savings go over 20 years to the Rio Lempa Conservation and Restoration Program, co-managed by Catholic Relief Services and FIAES, for conservation, water security and ecosystem restoration in the Lempa watershed; it serves the water standard.

items.name: FUSAL (Fundación Salvadoreña para la Salud y el Desarrollo Humano)
items.text: A Salvadoran foundation that runs early-childhood, education-quality and reading programmes, with more than 600 volunteers leading learning spaces for children in their communities; it reports that 91% of the children it serves improve their reading, comprehension and fluency. It works directly in 223 communities in all 14 departments and benefits more than 100,000 people a year.

items.name: Glasswing International
items.text: A non-profit that turns schools into community centres, with after-school clubs run by volunteer mentors, clubs for adolescent girls, a FabLab for young people and SanaMente, a mental-health programme for teachers and other frontline workers. It has worked with a school in Las Palmas, San Salvador, since 2010.

items.name: Kodigo
items.text: A technology academy founded in 2017 that trains Salvadorans in programming and artificial intelligence, with an AI tutor available around the clock; more than 1,780 people had taken part in its AI programmes by October 2026. With IDB Lab it ran a programming bootcamp for people in vulnerable situations, who paid nothing until they found a job in the technology sector.

items.name: FUNDASAL (Fundación Salvadoreña de Desarrollo y Vivienda Mínima)
items.text: A non-profit founded in 1968 that builds and improves homes with rural and urban communities through mutual aid, in which each family gives about 24 hours of work a week, which it says cuts costs by 55% against social housing built with industrial materials. It won a World Habitat Award in 2025 for work in 12 rural communities and two rural housing cooperatives, where 640 earth houses were built or improved for 2,708 people.

items.name: Hábitat para la Humanidad El Salvador
items.text: A housing organisation at work in El Salvador since 1992 that builds and improves homes to each family’s needs, financed by credit, credit with subsidy or subsidy. It served 106,322 people in its 2025 fiscal year, including 14,645 through incremental building and 2,170 through new homes.

items.name: SAC Optima
items.text: A lender to small businesses since 2009 that became a savings and credit society in 2024, able to take deposits under the supervision of the Superintendency of the Financial System; it serves about 20,000 clients through 16 branches, mostly micro, small and medium enterprises and informal sector workers. The Belgian development investor BIO, which lent it US$5 million in 2021, granted it technical assistance in October 2025.

items.name: Apoyo Integral
items.text: A microfinance institution, regulated since 2009, that lends to the upper micro segment and small enterprises through 26 branches and more than 440 payment points: 55% of its credit clients have no credit history in the regulated financial system, and 55% of its portfolio is in rural areas. BIO lent it US$10 million in 2020.
